stories.headline: Alternative for Germany wins state election in Saxony-Anhalt
stories.body:
The Alternative for Germany party won the state election in Saxony-Anhalt [c1]. The party is also known as the AfD [c1]. Outlets reported slightly different final vote totals for the winning party. Al Jazeera reported that the AfD finished on top with about 44% of the vote [c1]. The Times of India reported that the party won 44.5% of the vote [c7]. Preliminary election results showed that the party won 43.8% of the vote [c9]. Those preliminary results leave the party three seats short of an outright majority [c9].

Ulrich Siegmund is an AfD candidate in Saxony-Anhalt [c6]. Siegmund is 35 years old [c6]. He is a former fragrance salesman [c6]. Germany's domestic intelligence agency has closely watched the political group [c2]. The agency classified the AfD branch in Saxony-Anhalt as a proven right-wing extremist group [c2].

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke about the election results [c3]. Merz insists there can be no cooperation between mainstream parties and the AfD [c3]. Merz said the AfD victory was the worst electoral defeat his party had suffered in decades [c4]. His party is the Christian Democratic Union, known as the CDU [c4]. Merz said the defeat had shaken the CDU to its very foundations [c4].

Voter support for the CDU fell sharply during the state vote [c10]. Outlets reported different numbers for the party's final share. The Times of India reported that the Christian Democrats fell to 18.5% of the vote [c7]. The BBC reported that the CDU vote share almost halved to 17.2% [c10]. Voters expressed strong dissatisfaction with Merz during the vote [c5]. An exit poll in Saxony-Anhalt showed that only 9% of voters approved of Merz's performance [c5].

The state election outcome attracted international attention [c11]. US President Donald Trump posted a screenshot of the projected election results on Truth Social [c11]. In other European news, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni reached a political milestone [c8]. Meloni's administration has surpassed 1,413 consecutive days in office [c8].

vocab.meaning: A person who holds extreme political or religious views.
More than half of the total number.

stories.headline: Thousands attend Belgrade funeral for convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic
stories.body:
Mourners buried convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade [c12]. Thousands of people attended the service [c12]. Mladic died in The Hague at age 84 [c13]. He died while serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity [c13]. The United Nations war crimes court convicted Mladic of genocide over the 1995 Srebrenica massacre [c15]. Around 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys were killed in that massacre [c15].

Serbian Patriarch Porfirije personally officiated at the funeral service [c16]. The service took place at the St Luka church in Belgrade [c16]. Organizers provided free bus services from Bosnia and towns across Serbia for people attending [c20]. Fans of football club Red Star Belgrade displayed an image of Mladic before a match against Partizan Belgrade [c21]. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend the funeral [c17]. Vucic cited a scheduled meeting with the president of Uzbekistan [c17].

The military honors at the funeral drew international criticism. An EU spokesman said glorifying war criminals, denying genocide, and revisionism contradict fundamental European values [c14]. EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos canceled a planned visit to Belgrade after the funeral [c18]. In separate local news, a canopy collapse at a railway station in Novi Sad killed 16 people in November 2024 [c19]. That collapse triggered student-led protests in Serbia [c19].

vocab.meaning: Led or conducted an official or religious ceremony.
The reinterpretation of accepted historical facts.

stories.headline: Oil prices jump as shipping disruptions hit Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Global oil prices rose as military actions disrupted shipping routes in the Middle East [c22][c24]. Brent oil futures rose to around $97 a barrel [c22]. Brent crude is up 9% over five days [c22]. The price is also up 19% over the past month [c22]. US West Texas Intermediate crude rose to $92.27 a barrel [c23].

Military forces reported attacks on oil infrastructure and vessels [c24][c25]. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers [c24]. Iran's IRGC said it struck three tankers and three US-linked vessels [c24]. Saudi Aramco's Jizan facilities were struck for the second time in a month [c25].

The disruptions reduced shipping traffic through a key waterway [c29]. Macquarie analysts estimated that around 7 million barrels per day of crude and refined fuels cross the Strait of Hormuz [c29]. That volume is down from roughly 20 million barrels per day before the conflict [c29]. Iran and Oman are in the final stages of negotiating an agreement [c28]. The two countries want to establish a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz [c28].

Fuel costs increased for consumers in several countries [c26][c27]. The average US national petrol price reached $4.15 per gallon [c26]. US diesel prices reached over $5.90 per gallon [c26]. India's average crude oil import basket crossed $100 per barrel on Friday for the first time in six weeks [c27]. The price reached $101.07 [c27].

vocab.meaning: Financial contracts to buy or sell something at a set price later.
Unrefined petroleum straight from the ground.

stories.headline: US envoys hold peace talks with leaders in Russia and Ukraine
stories.body:
American envoys held separate peace talks over the weekend with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [c30]. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held discussions in Moscow and Kyiv [c30]. Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow first [c30]. The envoys then traveled to Kyiv by train from Poland [c34]. Putin declared a three-day ceasefire to ensure the safety of the visiting US envoys [c35].

Zelenskyy held three rounds of talks with the US envoys in Kyiv [c36]. National security advisers from the UK, France, and Germany joined the final round [c36]. Witkoff said on social media that substantive progress was made [c31]. He said the progress included movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks [c31]. Zelenskyy said Ukraine will need a winter package of military assistance if the war drags into winter [c37]. He said that package must include Patriot missile systems [c37].

The talks drew criticism within Ukraine. Ukrainian MP Lisa Yasko said Ukraine does not trust the talks [c33]. Yasko called the envoys' flattery towards Putin disgraceful [c33]. In separate human rights news, UN Human Rights Chief Volker Turk called for an urgent ban on fully autonomous weapons [c32]. Turk made the call after reports that autonomous drones killed people in Ukraine [c32].

vocab.meaning: Official representatives sent by a government on a diplomatic mission.

stories.headline: Israeli airstrikes kill dozens in southern Lebanon amid rising tensions
stories.body:
Israeli military strikes in southern Lebanon killed dozens of people over several days [c38][c42]. Lebanese health authorities reported that Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon killed at least 27 people over a three-day period [c42]. The Lebanese health ministry said 13 people died in one set of airstrikes, including women and children [c38].

An Israeli overnight strike hit a building in Kfar Rumman [c39]. That strike killed 11 people, including two children and four women [c39]. A second strike in Kfar Rumman killed an 18-year-old rescuer affiliated with the Amal movement [c40]. That second strike also wounded another person [c40].

The military strikes followed clashes along the border [c41][c44]. Two explosive drones were launched towards Israeli troops near the Ali al-Taher ridge [c44]. The Israeli military said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in response [c44]. Near the Beaufort fortress, a Hezbollah member opened fire during a close-quarters encounter [c41]. Two Israeli soldiers were lightly injured in that incident [c41].

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun commented on the military actions [c43]. Aoun called the strikes a dangerous escalation [c43]. He said the attacks jeopardize the June US-brokered ceasefire [c43].

vocab.meaning: An increase in the intensity or seriousness of a conflict.
Officially connected or associated with an organization.

stories.headline: Amazon cargo plane crashes past runway at Miami airport
stories.body:
An Amazon cargo plane crashed after overshooting the runway at Miami International Airport [c45]. The crash killed five people and injured five others [c45]. The aircraft was a Boeing 767-300 operated by 21 Air [c45].

The plane was operating as Amazon Air flight 7598 [c48]. It had flown from Cincinnati to Miami, then from Miami to San Juan [c48]. The crash occurred while the plane was returning from San Juan to Miami [c48].

The plane overran the runway and traveled approximately 1,300 feet past the end of the paved area [c46][c49]. It entered a perimeter area near where Tesla robotaxis were stationed [c49]. During the overshoot, the plane struck two vehicles [c46]. It hit a Ford van carrying seven contract cleaning workers [c46]. It also hit a Toyota Corolla carrying three passengers [c46].

Investigators have started looking into the cause of the crash. The NTSB recovered the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder from the aircraft [c47]. Safety features at the airport have also come under scrutiny [c50]. Miami International Airport is not equipped with engineered materials arresting systems at the end of its runways [c50].

vocab.meaning: Going beyond the intended landing area on a runway.
Critical and thorough examination or observation.

stories.headline: Seven dead after illegal hostel building collapses in Delhi
stories.body:
A building collapse in the Satya Niketan area of Delhi killed seven people [c55]. Reports gave different details about the age of the structure [c56][c68]. Livemint reported that the building was 55 years old [c56]. Scroll.in reported that the building was 40 to 50 years old [c68].

The five-storey building housed a boys' paying guest facility [c56]. The facility had two rooms per floor and two beds per room [c56]. A police source cited by PTI said the 55-square-metre structure had no columns or beams for support [c57]. Basement renovation work and water accumulation likely contributed to the collapse [c54].

Reports also differed on the number of people rescued from the rubble [c55][c68]. Livemint reported that rescue agencies rescued 12 people, of whom seven died [c55]. Scroll.in reported that 11 people were rescued [c68]. Scroll.in also reported that an estimated 30 to 35 students remained trapped under rubble [c68]. One victim was 19-year-old Arpit [c51]. Following his death, his family donated his corneas [c51].

Police launched a criminal investigation into the managers [c52][c58]. The property is registered in the name of 75-year-old Urmila Gupta [c52][c53]. Her husband, 81-year-old retired Indian Air Force Sergeant Hariram Gupta, managed the facility with their 52-year-old son Mahesh Gupta [c52][c53]. Delhi Police arrested all three family members [c52]. Scroll.in reported that the owner was arrested in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan [c70].

Police filed a case at the South Campus Police Station [c58]. Charges include culpable homicide, negligence in upkeep of a structure, and endangering safety [c58]. An alleged agreement signed by occupants said facility authorities were not responsible for casualties or compensation [c65]. The agreement claimed exemption from liability for sealing, fire, heavy rains, earthquakes, or natural calamities [c65].

The Municipal Corporation of Delhi, known as the MCD, had previously flagged the structure [c66]. The MCD identified it as an unauthorized four-storey building above ground level in a resettlement colony [c66]. Permission in that area was only granted for a single storey above ground level [c66]. Authorities suspended five municipal officials after the collapse [c69]. The Delhi government also ordered a citywide sealing of illegal five-storey buildings [c59].

Legal and political reactions followed the collapse [c60][c63]. The Delhi High Court directed the MCD to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level [c63]. A bench of Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia reviewed the case [c64]. The judges said responsibility extends to university authorities and the MCD [c64]. The judges said blame does not rest solely on the property owner [c64]. The court directed the MCD to audit paying guest facilities and hostels [c67]. It also asked Delhi University for details on outstation students and hostel capacity [c67].

Political groups demanded official action [c60]. The Cockroach Janta Party released a list of seven demands [c60]. Spokesperson Saurav Das called for a probe into the larger paying guest mafia and the construction of government hostels [c60]. Das requested compensation of up to 1 crore rupees for families of the deceased [c61]. He requested 20 lakh rupees for the injured [c61]. Das questioned Delhi Urban Development & Planning and Education Minister Ashish Sood [c62]. Das asked why 13 district committees created after a June 2026 hotel fire were wound down [c62].

vocab.meaning: Deserving blame or considered responsible for a wrong.
The illegal killing of one person by another.
Not having official permission or approval.
